solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Holy man and Yankee cross legendary river

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y
a cross is drawn as the letter X

explanation.surface: A saint and an American walk together over a river of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the dead were ferried across this river into the underworld.

clue.text: Philosopher's appeal for help acquiring case

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so the plea for help holds the case inside

blocks.note: SOS is the distress signal
a crate is a packing case

explanation.surface: A philosopher pleads for help to win his court case.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay. Socrates was famously tried and condemned in Athens, which gives the legal 'case' its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the classical Athenian thinker who taught Plato.

clue.text: Unknown bearing ingredient for bread?

blocks.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns
east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A mystery ingredient that gives bread its character.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is only one of the things it goes into; beer is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus added to dough to make bread rise.

clue.text: Mysterious European drunkard near Morecambe maybe

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a sot is a habitual drinker
Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise; 'maybe' marks him as one example of an Eric

explanation.surface: A puzzling continental boozer is spotted near the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort, but it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, so it seems obscure or mysterious to outsiders.

clue.text: Shout frantically over woman in a state

indicators.note: doing something frantically means wildly and without order, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Carol is a woman's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yells wildly at a woman who is in a real state.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means placed above, so the rearranged word sits on top of CAROL. 'In a state' reads as 'agitated', hiding the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: South Carolina is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Leader of tour on nameless African river's a dynamic individual

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the first letter of tour is taken
nameless means without a name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the Niger flows through West Africa

explanation.surface: A tour guide on a nameless African river turns out to be a live wire.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts T above the river with its N removed; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling an energetic, fiercely determined person a tiger is a common figurative usage.

clue.text: Fully understand some cereal is expensive

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next words

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone finally grasps that some breakfast cereal costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become fully aware of it or grasp it clearly.

clue.text: At the home of companion, meze is limitless

indicators.note: without limits means the word's boundaries, its first and last letters, are cut away

blocks.note: CH is a Companion of Honour, a British order
meze is a selection of Mediterranean small dishes

explanation.surface: At a friend's house, the platter of small dishes is endless.
explanation.walkthrough: MEZE loses its first and last letters to leave EZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Chez is a French preposition borrowed into English for 'at the house of'.

clue.text: Article for number one educationalist to review critically

blocks.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree, held by a teacher
to pan a show is to give it a bad review

explanation.surface: A top-rated item that a teacher must review harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like the best, but it is the nursery euphemism for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpan is a receptacle a bedridden patient uses to urinate, which is 'doing a number one' in childish slang.

clue.text: Church primate with gold hat

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
an ape is a primate
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An archbishop, the Church's primate, wears a gold hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop next to 'Church', but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for a hat, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Solemn place of burial

blocks.note: first meaning: serious in manner
second meaning: a hole where a body is buried

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of a cemetery; the two parts are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning serious and also a noun for a tomb dug in the ground.

clue.text: Current sheep cause trouble

blocks.note: AC is alternating current
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Sheep of the present day are being a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning modern, but it is electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is an idiom for misbehaving or making a fuss.

clue.text: Awful house with Rolls Royce inspector recalled

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the inspector's abbreviation is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
RR is the abbreviation for Rolls-Royce
DI is a detective inspector; it is turned round

explanation.surface: A dreadful house whose owner had his Rolls-Royce inspector called back.
explanation.walkthrough: Car makers recall faulty vehicles, which makes 'recalled' look like motoring news.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid is an informal synonym for very unpleasant or nasty.

clue.text: Sort of T-shirt nautical team swill

blocks.note: a ship's company is its crew
to neck a drink is British slang for gulping it down

explanation.surface: A type of T-shirt worn by sailors who drink heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swill' reads as pig food or rinsing water, but here it means drinking greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew neck is a round, close-fitting neckline, a common style of T-shirt and jumper.

clue.text: East wind unsettled country forecaster and artist

indicators.note: something unsettled is disturbed and not in its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for east
taken as written, then rearranged
a country is a land
a seer foretells the future

explanation.surface: An unsettled east wind over the country, as told by a weather forecaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The forecaster looks meteorological, but a seer forecasts the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter famous for animal pictures and sculptor of the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: Loaded spring no longer operative

blocks.note: a well is a spring of water
something switched off is no longer working

explanation.surface: A loaded spring mechanism that no longer works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' and 'spring' suggest a mechanism, but 'Loaded' means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very rich, and well-off means comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: Relaxing novel read on motor yacht

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht

explanation.surface: A soothing novel to read on board a motor yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book to read, but it is the anagram signal; 'on' in a down clue places the first part above MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy music or mood is soft and soothing, inducing a restful state.

clue.text: Learner to probe snooker equipment and complete game

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the learner's letter is pushed into the equipment

blocks.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker
L is for learner, as on L-plates
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: A beginner investigates snooker gear and finishes a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probe' suggests investigating, which fits the murder-mystery game, but here it only means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is the British name for the murder-mystery board game sold as Clue in North America.

clue.text: In East London, source of warmth yielding apple?

indicators.note: Cockney speech in East London drops the H sound from the start of words

blocks.note: a heater warms a room

explanation.surface: In the East End, a fire that produces an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys of East London traditionally drop their h's, so the warming device loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is an apple grown for eating raw rather than cooking; the question mark admits it is just one kind of eater.

clue.text: Jostle with the Spanish rower that's at front

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
in a rowing crew the bow is the oarsman seated nearest the front of the boat

explanation.surface: Pushing and shoving alongside a Spanish oarsman at the front of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The rower nearest the bow of a racing boat is called bow.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to push people aside with the arms, a verb synonym for jostle.

clue.text: Outlaw trade union language

blocks.note: to outlaw is to ban
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: Banning the language used by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is a large family of related African tongues, including Swahili and Zulu.

clue.text: Parisian who finally found money in England

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of found is kept

blocks.note: qui is French for who
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Parisian who at last found cash while in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid is British slang for one pound sterling.

clue.text: Stole tackle primarily on posh marine vehicle

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of tackle is used

blocks.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
a boa is a long scarf, a kind of stole
the opening letter of tackle

explanation.surface: Someone stole fishing tackle from a posh seagoing craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the past tense of steal, but it is the scarf. Wordplay reads BOA plus T placed after U.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German military submarine, a vessel that travels under the sea.

clue.text: Huge masculine chaps getting in Pilsner regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the beer name is kept
getting in means entering, so the chaps go inside the kept letters

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of the word
M is the abbreviation for masculine
chaps are men
the sixth letter of the word, completing its even letters

explanation.surface: Big manly blokes sinking a lager.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Pilsner give ISE, and M plus MEN go between its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense is a synonym for enormous, describing something of very great size.

clue.text: Dave's outside, wild about Republican postponement

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters only
about means surrounding, so the wild word goes round the party letter

blocks.note: first and last letters of the name
feral means wild, of an animal
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Dave is outside, raging at a Republican over a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dave's outside' reads as Dave standing outdoors, but it means just the edges of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferral is a putting-off of something until later, the same thing as a postponement.

clue.text: Get rid of flat-bottomed boat

blocks.note: first meaning: to throw away as worthless
second meaning: a Chinese sailing vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Reads as an instruction to scrap a boat; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for discarding and a noun for the traditional Chinese flat-bottomed sailing ship.
